name: Dinghy
notes: A fictional single-handed 4.2 m dinghy modelled on the ILCA (Laser), no spinnaker (#14).

Version 4 (#298): the backwind is a right trapezoid on her windward quarter, astern of the stern, following her heading and windward side (it swaps sides at the boom crossing): from the windward stern corner (0.63 m out, 0.15 hull lengths) 1 hull length out along the stern, 2 astern on its outer edge and 1.5 on its inner one (innerLengthHullLengths), the far edge slanting between. A boat in it loses up to 25% of her wind at the stern edge, fading to nothing at the far edge. Sizes and loss are placeholders for the owner's sliders (#232). Everything else is version 3's.
Units: knots, degrees, seconds, metres; shadow and backwind sizes in hull lengths.

Polar 6-20 kn: docs/research/ilca-dinghy-polars-and-handling.md section 7, except two cells: 165 deg at 8 kn is 5.2 (not 5.3) so the best downwind angle is 180 deg from 8 kn up, and 110 deg at 14 kn is 9.2 (not 9.1) so the reach's steepest gain starts at 12 kn (planing onset).

Version 2 (#71): the turn rate curve, rudder drag and no-go time constant are tuned so tacks and gybes cost what #14 asks: at 10 kn a tack takes about 3.5 s, bottoms out at about half its entry speed and loses about a hull length; a gybe loses a quarter to half a hull length.

Version 3 (#230, schema 2): the autohelm's steering values (ADR 0007, #219), all placeholders until they're tuned as debug sliders: the snap widths (3 deg upwind, 5 deg downwind, #230), the gain (full rudder at 10 deg of error), the dead-run margin (a 180 deg groove is sailed at 177 deg, the wind on the quarter away from the boom) and how far short of the by-the-lee limit it holds an angle by the lee. Everything else is version 2's.
Placeholders (JSON Pointers above) await tuning: the 0, 4 and 25 kn polar columns and every value the research and #14 give no number for.
